pages.text: An anomaly is a system, not a cell. A tumour builds a $(thing)microenvironment$(): blood vessels, fibroblasts, a stiffened matrix, immune cells talked into helping. Signalling networks - growth factors, cytokines, feedback loops - decide which cells divide, move or die, and a mutation in one hub rewires them all.

Seen from far away, it invades as a $(thing)front$(): cells of density u diffuse (D) and grow (r) until crowded, ∂u/∂t = D∇²u + ru(1 − u/K), and any small seed becomes a front moving at c = 2√(Dr). Fractured Reality does the same on the block grid - a $(thing)cellular automaton$(), each block catching from its neighbours - until the healing outruns the spread.
In the $(item)Bioreactor$(), a metastatic spore with stem cells and enzymes in broth and xenoplasm grows a $(item)Tumour Microenvironment Organoid$().
An anomaly is never alone: here it has grown its own blood vessels, recruited its own stroma and taught the local immune cells to look away.$(br2)Made in $(item)Bioreactor$().
